business_problem: Solocal needed to modernize PagesJaunes from a monolith and very large on-premises MongoDB deployment to a cloud-native architecture that reduced cost, simplified operations, and improved search and release speed.
solution_summary: Solocal evolved PagesJaunes from monolithic systems and one of the world's largest on-premises MongoDB deployments into a cloud-native microservices architecture on MongoDB Atlas running on Google Cloud. Atlas became the operational store for search, listings, maps, reviews, and asynchronous workflows, allowing Solocal to retire a separate Elasticsearch VM, a MongoDB-to-Elasticsearch mirror, and custom edge-case infrastructure. Automatic indexing, backup, restore, and auto-scaling reduced the operational burden while keeping all search data in one platform. By consolidating core data and search inside Atlas and MongoDB Search on Atlas, Solocal can answer millisecond user queries, provision releases far faster, and extend modern search-driven testing and directory experiences without maintaining separate clusters.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores PagesJaunes directory, review, map, and workflow data in Solocal's cloud-native platform.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Search on Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs integrated search so Solocal no longer needs a separate Elasticsearch stack for discovery workloads.

data_flow: Directory listings, maps, reviews, and asynchronous task data are stored in MongoDB Atlas on Google Cloud. MongoDB Search on Atlas indexes the same data for user-facing and internal search, eliminating the old mirror into Elasticsearch and allowing releases, testing, backup, and scaling to happen in one managed platform.
business_outcome: Solocal raised availability to 99.995%, cut database costs from 30% to 4% of the IT budget, reduced release work from a week by a team to one hour by one operator, and dramatically simplified search operations.
